cases.reason: The rule defers to relation conditions. The only part of 2002's comparison text that 2023 changed in substance is the numeric comparison under 2002 standard arithmetic (ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD, a mode 2023 removed): rounding to 31 digits on comparison. That case cannot change a condition-name result. A conditional variable has at most 31 digits (2002 PICTURE SR6). Its VALUE literals must fit its PICTURE. Float usages use native arithmetic in 2002. So both operands convert exactly and compare the same as in 2023. The alphanumeric, national, boolean and alphanumeric-national comparison texts are the same in substance (I compared 8.8.4.1.1.4 to .8 with 2023's 8.8.4.2.5 to .11). Probe r2 checks equality over a CD field (QNB=F).

cases.reason: The rule decides the sign of 'its value', the value of arithmetic-expression-1. In 2002 that value is computed by standard arithmetic when OPTIONS ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD is in effect: 32-digit truncation per operation, rounded to 31 digits for the comparison. 2023 removed ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD; its GR1 'rules of arithmetic in effect' means NATIVE, STANDARD-BINARY or STANDARD-DECIMAL. So the 2023 verdict says nothing about the 2002 standard-arithmetic case. Probe r4 at --std 2002 under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD: A=1.0000000000000001, C=1.0000000000000002. The exact A*A is 1+2E-16+1E-32 (33 digits), which truncates to 1+2E-16, so A*A-C is 0. 2002 requires POSITIVE false and ZERO true. Observed: POS=T ZERO=F, a 34-digit result (the same as r4b at 2023 under STANDARD-DECIMAL). This is the known 34-digit standard-arithmetic defect at --std 2002 reaching the sign condition. compiler-at-2002: wrong.

cases.reason: Item c) orders indexed records by 'a given key of reference'. In 2002 the prime and alternate record keys may be subscripted table elements: 5.1.3 lets data-name-n carry subscription, 2002 RECORD KEY SR1 and ALTERNATE RECORD KEY SR1 add only 'may be qualified', and 2014 E.2 item 25 records that later editions added the OCCURS prohibition. 2023 RECORD KEY SR1 forbids OCCURS, so the 2023 evidence never has a subscripted key of reference. The compiler refuses such keys at --std 2002 (COBOL2024; refute-p-01/reckey.cbl). Items a) and b) are covered. It would be settled by deciding whether the subscripted-key defect (filed against the RECORD KEY rows from p-01) needs its own sequential-order witness for this rule once it is fixed.

cases.reason: This rule names the relative key data item and the record key data item. In 2002 both may be subscripted table elements: 5.1.3 allows subscription for data-name-n, 2002 RELATIVE KEY SR1 and RECORD KEY SR1 say only 'may be qualified', and 2014 E.2 item 25 records the OCCURS prohibition as added after 2002. 2023 RELATIVE KEY SR1 and RECORD KEY SR1 forbid OCCURS, so 2023 GR3 never governs random access through a subscripted key, and its verdict says nothing about that 2002 case. Probe r5 at --std 2002 (RELATIVE KEY IS RK(2), RK OCCURS 3 in working-storage, ACCESS RANDOM) is refused with COBOL2024, and so is RECORD KEY IS K(2) (refute-p-01/reckey.cbl). compiler-at-2002: wrong. It refuses legal 2002 source, so random access by a subscripted key cannot run. The root is the same defect as p-01's RECORD KEY overturn, which this probe extends to RELATIVE KEY.
